'''John David Crawford''' (1954&ndash;1998)<ref name="PAW" /> was an American physicist and professor at the [[University of Pittsburgh]].<ref name="PAW">{{cite news|url=https://paw.princeton.edu/memorials/43/28/index.xml|title=John David Crawford '77|date=June 9, 1999|publisher=[[Princeton Alumni Weekly]]|accessdate=20 May 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222153831/https://paw.princeton.edu/memorials/43/28/index.xml|archivedate=22 December 2015}}</ref> He obtained his undergraduate degree with honors from [[Princeton University]] in 1977
and his Ph.D. from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1983.<ref name="PAW" />

An internationally recognized researcher in [[theoretical physics]], he specialized in [[plasma physics]] and [[nonlinear dynamics]].<ref name="DS">{{cite journal|last=Knobloch|first=Edgar|date=October 1998|title=1954–1998|url=http://www.dynamicalsystems.org/ag/pr/getfile?item=1102|url-status=dead|journal=[[Dynamical Systems Magazine]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305111424/http://www.dynamicalsystems.org/ag/pr/getfile?item=1102|archive-date=5 March 2016|access-date=8 July 2021}}</ref>
His broad physical insight and deep knowledge of mathematics enabled him to make profound contributions to [[dynamical system]]s.<ref name="DS" />
He published more than 80 research papers and wrote a landmark review on [[bifurcation theory]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Crawford|first=John David|title=Introduction to bifurcation theory|date= 1 October 1991|journal=[[Reviews of Modern Physics]]|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|volume=63|issue=4|doi=10.1103/revmodphys.63.991|pages=991–1037|bibcode=1991RvMP...63..991C|url=https://repositories.lib.utexas.edu/bitstream/2152/61063/1/Crawford_1991.pdf|hdl=2152/61063|hdl-access=free}}</ref> Additionally, he was also a codirector of the "Research Experiences for Undergraduates" program, which exposed undergraduates to scientific study, in 1997.<ref name="PAW" />

Apart from his research, he was a passionate mountain climber. He died on August 23, 1998, at the [[UPMC Montefiore|Montefiore Hospital]] in [[Pittsburgh]] of [[Burkitt's lymphoma]], a form of lymph cancer.<ref name="PAW" />

In 2001, [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]'s [[Activity Group in Dynamical Systems]] established the [[J.D. Crawford Prize]], which is now the world's top
award in dynamical systems.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/crawford.php|title=J.D. Crawford Prize (SIAG/Dynamical Systems)|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]|accessdate=20 May 2015}}</ref>
